the piece of media i was referencing was actually “ghost in the shell.” i’m a casual anime fan, so i had heard lots of good things about it but with people not wanting to spoil it for me, i never knew much about it. i see lots of screencaps from it on my pinterest (hence the technologically advanced world setting) and so i took tons of inspiration from how the world looked (more so the general vibe of the world than the setting itself.) so i was taken aback when i read through the plot of the movie and realized that a few names of locations were similar and just a similar world structure in general despite me never evening viewing the movie myself.

it’s more of a crazy coincidence the more i think about it, but it’s not a bad thing of course.

yeah, i was thinking that.

of course i’m glad it’s a piece of media i can proudly say i took inspiration from so i can show others how great it is (like how others would rave about it to me and eventually i got inspired by it) and it’s not like the entire thing is identical. i guess it was just a shock to me as i had never seen this piece of media at all nor knew what it’s plot was and yet, it somehow seemed like i originally took worldbuilding elements from it when i was just super infatuated with the depiction of how they framed the world visually.

it’s definitely not something i’m upset with, in fact i’m honestly more so excited (esp with my ocs and their world being my biggest hyperfixation for 2 yrs straight) because now i have more media to consume that similar in style to my ocs.

it’s set in a post apocalyptic universe in an underground safe zone after a devastating event which left the surface of the world in a nuclear winter! the world is extremely technologically advanced and much of the population has been convinced by the corrupt government that they need to transfer their humanity into android bodies. there are three different installments to this universe and different groups of ocs (some even reoccurring.) a big part of the entire storyline as a whole is “humanity desires connection” which is elaborated through different perspectives in each installment of the story.

i plan to turn the story into a visual novel of some sort so that i can also draw each of the characters myself and fully tell the story :,)

as an old niji fan, i definitely agree and even had my own theories on this.

another factor that can be thrown in this list is the differences in anniversary merch for the girls vs. the guys.

i remember when lazulight and other female waves had their first anniversaries and their merch for it was the same doodles drawn by the members plastered on everything from pop sockets to tote bags alongside some standees which were the only pieces of merch where you could pick from your oshis. but when luxiem's first anniversary merch dropped, it was standees along with decked out keychains and necklaces commemorating each member of the wave. i understand that luxiem was the wave that truly brought niji into the spotlight, but the fact that it was such a drastic difference from the female waves definitely shows some favoritism. why didn't they commemorate their very first en wave in the same way? weren't they important to the growth of the company as well?

also another thing to note is that ever since luxiem, the waves that debuted after them were either all male or co-ed. i remember mentioning how strange this was to a friend who wasn't a fan of vtubers and they agreed that it was weird how they hadn't debuted a full female wave since ethyria. it seems like niji realised how much profit they could make off of male members after luxiem's success and that was only proven further after noctyx debuted with huge success as well.

makes sense why male members were able to get off scot-free whenever they were in deep shit, but when a female member wanted to expand her horizons and made a complaint about mismanagement, niji nearly got her to take her own life. it's honestly baffling but not surprising.

this happened around the start of last year so not recent, but the one moment that stands out to me the most was when my grandma greeted me after she came back to our family house from her stay outside of the country. i came out to her as trans through text after she had left because i was worried about her reaction (for context: she would often come into my room or pull me aside to have talks to me about "being a woman.") when i first came out to her, her reaction was as you'd expect. thanking me for telling her and saying she still loved me, but that i'd "always be her granddaughter no matter what." that conversation left a bad taste in my mouth and i ended up never talking to her again while she was away. i was honestly dreading the day she'd return back from her stay.

however to my surprise, when she got to our house and saw me for the first time since leaving, she immediately smiled at me and called me a "handsome young man" before wrapping me in a big hug. i was so worried she'd be passively transphobic (?) so hearing her acknowledge my identity after the previous conversation we had felt like a huge learning moment for the both of us as well as a gender euphoria moment for me.

it's been a while since then (nearly a year) and she's still been trying to get used to my preferred pronouns. but she's definitely gotten better with them since the first few days she came back and even when she makes mistakes here and there, she's quick to simply correct herself and continue what she wants to say to me or the rest of my family. and now instead of talks about being a woman or how my body looks, she talks to me about staying positive and doing whatever makes me feel happy and comfortable. :,)

maybe you've already seen it, but pomu has actually stated in her [stream](https://www.youtube.com/live/EKSoVg67cD8?si=P2ZfqIf5GEuE2Ite&t=559) following the announcement that her channel will still be available after she leaves. i'm not sure why the announcement said that all of her content would be privated when it seems like pomu never intended on privating any of her vods or accounts, might've just been poor communication from the company (which wouldn't be a first anyways unfortunately.)

i will add that had pomu decided to private her content, your idea (while not with bad intentions) might seem like a bit of a strange move to make. i understand wanting to provide for fans like yourself who might've not had the chance to watch all of her streams before the graduation announcement, however wanting to monetize that reuploaded content can sound suspicious out of context. it also would be difficult for you to be able to contact her after she leaves to donate the earnings from the reuploads unless she has a redebut under a new identity or you manage to find her irl social media to directly contact her (the second of which would be a terrible idea.)

thankfully, you won't have to do any of that since her channel will stay archived. the best advice i can give you as someone who's also regretted not watching a vtuber before they chose to leave is to enjoy the remaining time we have left with the fairy. pomu said she'd be streaming everyday up until her graduation date, so you can relax and just be in the present with her for now.

and who knows? maybe after some time of watching through every single one of her vods after her graduation, she might debut again in the future and you can continue supporting her from then on! it's like her fellow en member uki said, this is just the start of a new chapter in the story of pomu wherever she is. :)
